post.caption: Particles bounced back off gold foil. At Manchester, Hans Geiger and student Ernest Marsden worked for Ernest Rutherford. They fired particles at a very thin sheet of gold foil and counted the flashes on a screen through a microscope. The plum pudding model of the atom predicted only small deflections, but a few particles bounced almost straight back. Rutherford said it was like a huge shell bouncing back off tissue paper. The experiments ran in 1908 and 1909, and in 1911 he placed the atom's positive charge in a tiny nucleus.
